# Generated by Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic)
Design — from FT (Fish Task) to a task model for schedulability analysis
=========================================================================
Written 2026-08-17 (brainstorm with Fatih, no code). Companion to
notes/join_semantics_from_traces.txt, notes/CRITICAL_autoware_intraprocess_waitables.txt
and the Aug-2026 handoff (open question "SAG-Nasri JSON directly vs an
intermediate representation").

Starting point
--------------
A task is NOT a callback. A task is the graph in which the callback is a
node. What FISH produces today that is closest to that object is the FT: a
weakly connected component of the L3 (callback) graph over DATA edges (infra
topics excluded, join membership ties included, ext boundary nodes as
sources/sinks). Everything measured in the last two days (Waitables, the two
delivery paths of a subscription, the bimodal cost of a join, trigger vs
data dependency) says the same thing: the information a task model needs is
in the trace, but the FT does not yet CARRY it explicitly. Four soft spots
of "FT = task", and a decision for each.

1. Boundaries — where does a task start and end?
------------------------------------------------
A WCC is "everything that touches". A real-time task has SOURCES (timers,
sensor / bag inputs, ext sources) and SINKS (actuators, ext sinks, or the
input of another task). In r10b the concat output feeds both perception
(centerpoint → objects) and localization (downsample → NDT → pose): the WCC
makes them ONE FT (71 F). One task, or two tasks forking at concat? In a
DAG-task model this is one DAG with a fork node; for analysis the two
branches carry different deadlines.
  DECISION: keep both levels. FT = the DAG task. Inside an FT, enumerate
  CHAINS = source→sink paths (Autoware's own "pipeline latency" notion is a
  chain). Deadlines are attached to chains, precedence/structure to the FT.

2. Joins — their place in the DAG
---------------------------------
What we measured on concatenate_data / gyro_odometer IS the DAG-task
AND-precedence node: the merge job cannot start before all N predecessors
have delivered. Today the model records membership (join ties, join_role).
A DAG-task model needs "N jobs → 1 job" precedence AND the merge cost as its
OWN job: the measurement is already bimodal (deposit ~30 µs, merge+publish
~25 ms, paid by whichever input is last).
  DECISION: split the join into deposit jobs (one per input F, cheap) and one
  MERGE job (heavy) with AND-precedence from all deposits (+ the timeout
  timer as an alternative trigger). The trace supports the split: deposit =
  callback_start of the input F; merge end = the publish (rcl_publish /
  publish_link inside the completer); merge start ≈ from the completer's
  window (exact start needs collector identity → Yol B uprobes). Do NOT bury
  the merge in the completer's WCET — it would overstate the deposit path
  700x and hide the join.

3. Period and multi-rate
------------------------
Task period = source period. concat: three lidars at the same rate → one
period. gyro_odometer: IMU 100 Hz + vehicle twist 30 Hz → output ≈ 100 Hz
(826/851). What is the period of a multi-source DAG?
  DECISION: do not force a period. Take the RELEASE PATTERN of the source
  jobs from the trace (per_instance mode gives it) and let AND-joins release
  the merge job; the analyzer (SAG) consumes job release times/jitter, which
  is exactly what Nasri's job-set format expects. Period is a derived,
  optional summary (timer-driven sources have one; sensor-driven ones have
  a measured min/max inter-arrival).

4. Executor mapping
-------------------
An FT's jobs run on different executors/threads/processes: pointcloud_container
is a 20-thread MultiThreadedExecutor, the per-lidar preprocessors are
single-threaded containers, the velodyne wrapper is another process. So a
"task" is a DAG spread over executors — global scheduling with precedence,
each executor with its own policy (rclcpp executor dispatch order, thread
count, callback groups). This is FISH's L0/L1 layer already.
  DECISION: every job carries its executor (and callback group / thread pool
  size) in the task model; the analyzer decides how to treat executors as
  processors. Never flatten this into a single-processor task.

The resulting definition (proposed)
-----------------------------------
  "An FT is a DAG task of the data-trigger graph. Its jobs are the F's
   (with joins split into deposit jobs + a merge job). Its precedence
   constraints are the data edges and the AND-joins (timeout timers as
   alternative releasers). Every job carries its executor. Source→sink
   paths inside the FT are chains, and deadlines are attached to chains."

Consequences
------------
- This maps directly onto a Nasri-style job set + precedence DAG (SAG
  input): job = (F instance, release from trace, BCET/WCET by ROLE, executor),
  precedence = data edge or AND-join.
- Answer to the handoff's open question ("emit SAG-compatible Nasri JSON
  directly, or build an intermediate representation first?"):
  IR = Intermediate Representation — the compiler-world term for a model
  that sits between the source (here: raw traces) and the target output
  (here: the analyzer's job-set JSON) and depends on neither. The FISH graph
  (PG graph_nodes / graph_edges + measured attributes: layers, data edges,
  join membership, delivery path, per-role timing, phase, GPU ownership,
  executor mapping, ext boundaries) IS that IR. It already exists. Nasri
  JSON is DERIVED from it by an emitter (extract_taskset.py is the seed;
  add join split + release patterns). Keep both: the IR is what the viz,
  the probe-effect harness and the paper figures read; the JSON is what
  SAG reads; a new analyzer format = a new emitter, not a new parser. The
  IR must carry what the trace could NOT supply as explicit unknown/approx
  (data-without-trigger dependencies, exact merge start) — the emitter
  closes those with an assumption or a user input, never silently.
- Case 1a/1b nodes (see join_semantics_from_traces.txt) need no split:
  ordinary message-hop precedence (1a) or a timer job with buffered inputs
  (1b).
- What the trace cannot supply (data-without-trigger dependencies, exact
  merge start) is marked as such in the IR; Yol B (uprobes) is the
  optional instrument that fills it.

Open for the next brainstorm
----------------------------
- Chain enumeration rule: all source→sink simple paths (explodes on
  fan-out) vs "named" chains (Autoware topics of interest) vs longest-path
  per sink.
- BCET/WCET per ROLE for every F (deposit/complete/timeout) as first-class
  attributes; today only join_analysis prints them.
- How the merge job's executor is chosen when the completer varies (it runs
  wherever the last input's callback runs — i.e. the merge job inherits the
  executor of a data-dependent predecessor). Model as "executor of the
  releasing job".
- Timeout timer as an alternative releaser: OR of (AND-join, timer) — check
  that SAG's precedence model can express it, or pre-expand into two job
  variants.
